about: The rules of spec/transforms/terrain_edit.md: one shard of the BFBC2 tool suite specification's rule index, written by spec/trace.py --emit; checked by spec/trace.py --check.

evidence.ref: spec/probes/terrain.py, 2026-11-22: 30 terrain partitions: TerrainData 30, TerrainHeightfieldData 53, TerrainHeightfieldGridCellInfo 43, TerrainFullDecal 314 (MaskTextureType TmttStandard 194, TmttArea 69, TmttNone 51), TerrainGroupDecal 80, TerrainSplineDecal 416, TerrainQuadDecal 40; every decal material / spline reference in no bundle

rules.title: The terrain partition is DICE's editor source; the game draws the baked resources

evidence.ref: from RNDR-TERR-2 (normals from height samples), RNDR-TERR-5 (the engine writes the height scale), DSTR-TERR-2 (the engine writes the destruction mask), TERR-VT-3 (rule layers have no tile) and TEDIT-SRC-1 (the resources are what is drawn)

rules.title: What an edit writes, and what the game makes itself

evidence.ref: spec/probes/terrain.py, 2026-11-22: 30 main blocks: n 1,024 x 11, 2,048 x 19; grid spacing 1 m on 30; min y 0 on 30

rules.title: DICE's main blocks are 1,024 or 2,048 samples of 1 m, starting at height 0

evidence.ref: spec/probes/terrain.py, 2026-11-22: per main block (terrain, n, range) as listed; TerrainHeightfieldData.SizeY counts as listed

rules.title: The height range is per level; DICE's are 395 - 1,700 m

evidence.ref: TERR-HF-4 - TERR-HF-11's grammars; the console and BF1943 converters keep the tails as they are (TERR-HF-7, TERR-HF-8)

rules.title: The derived parts of a height field are rewritten from the heights

evidence.ref: RNDR-TERR-5; pcbuild.ENGINE_NAMED lists the constant among those the engine writes by name
OPFOR's Wake Island install, 2026-11-07 onward: its patch shaders cloned from mp_009cq (range 500 m) draw its 1,000 m terrain; spec/probes/terrain.py: MP_009 500 m

rules.title: The height scale the patch shaders use is the engine's, not the database's

evidence.ref: spec/probes/terrain.py, 2026-11-22: (W, non-zero flags = tiled count): (128, yes) 305,154, (128, no) 6,142, (64, yes) 41,608, (64, no) 3,448, (16 / 8 / 4, yes) 3,072 / 5,376 / 3,072; every mismatch a rule-only shader (tiled 0) with 1 flag (MP_002 343, SP_009 4,804, NAM_MP_002R 3,000 ...)

rules.title: A painted cell writes its shader index, its tiles and its flags together

evidence.ref: rust/bc2-levelwrite/tests/terrain_layers.rs on the game copy, 2026-11-23: 23 Dist visual terrains, 7 one kind per layer; slot order 1,131 of 1,131 blocks and layers in name order, 1,063 of 1,463 reversed

rules.title: A shader's layers come from its name; a cell's tile slots are its tiled layers in that order

evidence.ref: spec/probes/terrain.py, 2026-11-22: 30 visual terrains, 1 atlas each; atlas (size, format, mips) against the header: 2048 x 1024 fmt 10 1 mip / (31, 15) x 5, 1024 x 512 / (15, 7) x 13, 1024 x 1024 / (15, 15) x 12, each = size / 64 - 1

rules.title: One mask-tile atlas per terrain, laid out as its patch maps' header says

evidence.ref: spec/probes/terrain.py and a per-terrain count (SPG2 scratch), 2026-11-22: 94,603 tiled masks, 79,973 in their tile's one block; per terrain the flags and the one shared tile as listed

rules.title: A tile covers a block of flag x flag cells; DICE's flags are 2 - 64

evidence.ref: spec/probes/terrain.py, 2026-11-22: patch shaders per terrain 7 - 109; layer counts 1: 48, 2: 194, 3: 344, 4: 424, 5: 328, 6: 152, 7: 24, 8: 1; tiled counts 0: 177, 1: 410, 2: 478, 3: 321, 4: 129
RNDR-TERR-1 (the entry per cell) and SHDB-LVL-1 (a level draws through its own databases only)

rules.title: A painted layer combination needs a patch shader entry in every database
A donor patch shader must match the tiled layers and the atlas layout
Rule-only patches need both patch layouts

evidence.ref: TERR-MM-2 - TERR-MM-4; the pairing of visual layers with materials is the editor's choice (no field links them in DICE's resources)

rules.title: Painting a physics material writes the material map's cells

evidence.ref: rust/bc2-levelwrite/tests/terrain_layers.rs on the game copy, 2026-11-23: MP_005's five tiled layers paired as listed

rules.title: The visual / material pairing is measured on the terrain's own cells

evidence.ref: spec/probes/terrain.py, 2026-11-22: blocks per terrain {1: 14, 13: 12, 25: 1, 37: 2, 49: 1}; 318 patch maps

rules.title: Main block, then a ring of 12 per ring
A sculpt that reaches the ring is stitched as DICE stitches its rings
The colour / occlusion map under an edit is re-baked by ratio
The editor's brushes write stored heights and cells, clamped to the range

evidence.ref: the terrain bundle's entries (heightfield, material map, visual terrain, water, atlas) hold no collision resource; the sampler reads the height field (`inputs::heightfield_of`)

rules.title: A sculpted level's path data is sampled on the staged height field

evidence.ref: rust/bc2-levelwrite/tests/new_terrain.rs on the game copy, 2026-11-27: 30 of 30 DICE main blocks (Dist's and Package's levels, bundles before 2013) through the import give DICE's stored samples, bounds and min / max tree

rules.title: A height map is stored from 0 m, its values kept as they are
A new level carries its own terrain under its own name, its base's left out

evidence.ref: rust/bc2-levelwrite/tests/new_terrain.rs on the game copy with MP_005 prepared for NavKit, 2026-11-27: as given; rust/BENCHMARKS.md E7-TG3

rules.title: A new level's path data is sampled and built on its own ground
A new terrain is sculpted and painted as the base's is, under the base's names
